Curator Backtest (CBT)

2023-07-24 to 2026-07-22

The watchlist-curator agent was called biweekly over the 2023-07-24 to 2026-07-22 window. At each rebalance it read a date-clean news pool for the preceding biweekly window (built upstream from GDELT GKG + Wayback, look-ahead-reduced; browse them in the pool browser) and proposed adds and removes against the active watchlist; the optimizer then ran mean-variance on the revised watchlist. Each rebalance is marked by an orange square on the curator curve in chart 2 — hover over one to see that rebalance's adds, removes, and the curator's rationale. The buy-and-hold curve below is the value of the initial portfolio (which never gets rebalanced or optimized) over time. The buy-and-hold portfolio has equal amounts of [AAPL, GOOGL, AMZN] and is held without any rebalancing across the window. Throughout the charts below: general_markets = defensive equity ETFs (broad-market / dividend / utilities / staples); cashlike = bonds + cash-equivalents + precious metals (e.g., AGG, BIL, IAU).

9. Gain per article vs news source

Plot 8's total gain per source divided by how many articles that source contributed to the pools (its footprint, shown as N art.). Signal density: high = a source that produced gains from few articles; near-zero/negative with many articles = low-signal, a block-list candidate.

10. Gain per article by lede source

Plot 9's gain per article (total forward gain / pool-article footprint), but bucketed by the LEDE SOURCE of the cited evidence: clean, look-ahead-safe Wayback ledes vs the look-ahead-biased live-fallback ledes (fetched from today's page). If live noticeably beats Wayback, the bias is flattering the picks — a caution on fuller-mode backtest returns.
